dct_description_sm: St.Louis has been quantifying export of total mercury (THg; all forms of Hg in a sample) and methyl mercury (MeHg; the toxic and bioaccumulative form of Hg) from the East and West catchments at Cape Bounty, as well as from a few smaller tributaries on the landscape, some of which have been impacted by major permafrost slumping.  St.Louis has also been quantifying the net ecosystem exchange (NEE) of carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) from aquatic surfaces at Cape Bounty since 2007 to determine if these systems are sources or sinks of these two gases with regards to the atmosphere.  NEE is a measure of the net balance between primary productivity and decomposition in systems.
dct_title_s: Mercury and Greenhouse Gas Concentrations in Streams/Lakes at the Cape Bounty Arctic Watershed Observatory, Melville Island
